result.title: HEART: Hierarchical Expert Adaptive Refinement Transformer for ECG Representation Learning
result.summary: Learning robust representations from electrocardiograms (ECGs) is challenging because repeated cardiac cycles coexist with subtle and sparse diagnostic cues in local morphology and rhythm-level context. Existing ECG foundation models commonly rely on Transformerbased patch encoders with uniformly shared dense refinement pathways, limiting adaptive processing across heterogeneous ECG tokens. We propose HEART (Hierarchical Expert Adaptive Refinement Transformer), an ECG foundation model that introduces stage-specific conditional expert refinement during self-supervised pre-training. HEART places a local-level MoE over patch-level representations before temporal contextualization and a global-level MoE over context-integrated token representations after self-attention. Token-level Top-1 routing allows different patches or contextual tokens within the same ECG to follow different expert pathways. On public ECG benchmarks, HEART achieves strong performance under both linear probing and fine-tuning, with particularly large frozen-encoder gains on PTB-XL Form and Rhythm (+6.76 AUROC points each over the strongest protocol-reproduced baseline). Routing analyses provide qualitative evidence of complementary local and global expert specialization. We release our code and pretrained models at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/HEART-5E9F.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 HEART，一个 ECG 基础模型，在自监督预训练中于时序上下文建模前后分别设置局部与全局 MoE，对 patch 级和上下文 token 做 Top-1 路由以实现分阶段的条件专家精化。
